test: Define active customer-year = customer with >=1 order in year Y (2016-2024); lapsed = no order in Y+1. Compute lapse rate by customer's current branch and current account manager (rep_id), with Wilson/binomial intervals and a chi-square-style comparison vs pooled rate. Control for size (prior-year revenue quintile/order-count band) and trade by computing expected lapses per branch/rep from pooled size x trade cells (indirect standardization), then observed/expected ratios. Check new vs established customers (onboarded_day), and friction (short lines, returns, invoice-question contacts) of lapsers vs non-lapsers within size bands. Size money from prior-year revenue of lapsers and the excess above expected.
support: Several branches or reps with observed/expected lapse well outside binomial noise (e.g. O/E > 1.3 with intervals excluding 1) persisting across years; lapse rising with friction within size bands.
weaken: O/E ratios for branches and reps within ~binomial noise of 1 after size/trade control; lapse concentrated in small/new customers; friction no higher among lapsers once size is controlled.
expect: Moderately confident (~65%) the hypothesis does NOT hold: the data look generated with even assignment (inside reps split evenly), so lapse is likely driven by customer size (small accounts lapse most) and spread evenly across branches/reps. Rep snapshot also limits rep attribution.
